_description: Material library recipe extracted from /Game/VFX/NiagaraDissolveEdge/Materials. Use this to teach ForgePilot how this folder organizes visual logic for portal rims, lightning arcs, radial energy sprites, masked motion shapes, smoke support, and grounded surface references.
overview: This library is centered around radial edge reads, dissolving/noisy portal rings, simple energy sprites, and a few support references for smoke, ice, rock, and masked motion silhouettes. The key lesson is that strong VFX visuals here come from separating visual roles: radial edge, arc line, support smoke, masked animated silhouette, and grounded surface reference are all different material families.
library_design_rules: Do not treat the folder as one unified look. It is a small visual library with several distinct roles.
Radial edge materials should prioritize silhouette and threshold logic before detail noise.
Lightning and line energy should prioritize directional read and motion first, not full-surface glow.
Masked animated silhouette materials should stay separate from generic additive sprite logic.
Grounded surface references like rock or ice are support references, not default choices for Niagara sprite particles.

radial_energy_edge.purpose: Circular rims, star cores, ring edges, aura bursts, and dissolving circular energy shapes.
dominant_logic: radial coordinate space or radial gradient logic
optional depth fade or noise breakup
ring or core read before secondary detail
selection_rules: Use M_Portal when the read should be a noisy ring or portal rim.
Use M_Star when the read should be a compact additive radial burst or bright star-like core.
Use M_CA when the look needs a synthetic energy shape driven more by math than by texture.

arc_and_lightning_line.purpose: Lightning-like line energy, animated arc strips, and aggressive directional energy flow.
dominant_logic: color dodge or aggressive additive composition
WorldPositionOffset support for unstable line motion
selection_rules: Use M_Lightning for arc energy, jagged line strips, or animated electrical edge motion.
Prefer this family when the read must feel directional and unstable rather than circular.

masked_motion_shape.purpose: Animated masked silhouettes with emissive support and WPO motion.
dominant_logic: radial or object-pivot aware motion support
selection_rules: Use this family when the visual identity comes from the silhouette itself, not from soft translucent glow.
Keep masked animated motifs separate from generic spark or portal materials.

soft_support_volume.purpose: Soft translucent support smoke or haze around the hero read.
dominant_logic: support role rather than hero shape
selection_rules: Use this as a support layer only.
Do not use this material family to carry the primary portal or energy silhouette.

grounded_surface_reference.purpose: Surface-bound grounded materials used as environmental or dissolve-target references rather than as Niagara sprite defaults.
selection_rules: Use these as mesh or target-surface references, not as portal/spark sprite materials.
M_Ice is useful when a dissolve-edge effect needs a frozen target aesthetic or emissive ice cracking support.
M_Rock is a neutral grounded reference for hard-surface dissolve targets.

dual_threshold_ring.description: Build a ring by subtracting an inner threshold from an outer threshold on top of a noisy radial field.

compact_additive_core.description: A very small graph can still produce a strong burst/core read if the radial gradient and emissive are clean.

procedural_energy_shape.description: Procedural math-driven shapes can replace texture dependence for synthetic magical or chromatic effects.

animated_arc_strip.description: A line or strip effect can be sold by layered panners, aggressive blend mode, and unstable deformation.

masked_animated_motif.description: Use a masked silhouette plus WPO when the motif itself must stay recognizable while moving.

soft_support_haze.description: Support smoke should stay soft and unobtrusive, reinforcing the main effect rather than replacing it.

if_the_effect_needs.need: portal rim or circular energy gate
bright core burst or magical star center
soft portal haze or dissolve support smoke
grounded mesh reference for dissolve target

authoring_guidance_for_forgepilot: When a prompt asks for a portal or ring edge, begin with radial_energy_edge logic, not with generic sprite panning.
When a prompt asks for lightning or crackling line energy, prefer the arc_and_lightning_line family rather than adapting a portal material.
Keep masked motif materials separate from translucent sprite materials.
Use support smoke only as a secondary layer around the hero edge or portal read.
Use rock and ice as dissolve-target or environment reference materials, not as default Niagara particle materials.
common_failure_modes: using portal-ring logic for line lightning
using a soft smoke material as the main portal silhouette
trying to get a crisp masked motif out of a generic translucent energy material
using grounded opaque surface materials as if they were sprite VFX parents
letting noise or smoke replace the primary edge silhouette

agent_recipe.step_1: Classify the requested visual into one of these roles: radial edge, line arc, masked motif, soft support haze, or grounded surface reference.
agent_recipe.step_2: Choose the closest material family from this library before proposing graph edits.
agent_recipe.step_3: Preserve the family-defining logic: radial thresholds for portal/ring, directional panning for lightning, masked silhouette for motif, soft opacity for support haze, surface shading for grounded targets.
agent_recipe.step_4: Expose art-facing parameters where possible when adapting these graphs, because the source library relies heavily on hard-coded values.
agent_recipe.step_5: Split one effect into multiple material roles instead of trying to force one material family to solve all visual problems.

known_reusability_risks: Most materials in this folder expose few or no artist-facing parameters. ForgePilot should treat them as logic references first, not as final reusable parents.
Several graphs rely on hard-coded textures or constants; future reusable versions should promote those to parameters.
M_Portal, M_Lightning, and M_CA are especially useful as logic patterns, but should be rebuilt with MI-friendly controls if used as production bases.
